blocks.markdown: A chattel mortgage secures a debt with **personal property while possession generally remains with the mortgagor**, subject to the **Chattel Mortgage Law (Act No. 1508)** and **Civil Code Arts. 2140–2141**. Act No. 1508 calls for the **prescribed mortgage instrument and description, affidavit of good faith, and registration requirements** for effectiveness against third persons. Check the **actual statutory text and any registration system** affecting the particular collateral.

**Reasonable description rule (Act No. 1508, Sec. 7):** the document must **describe the mortgaged property sufficiently to identify it**. A **vague catch-all may not adequately identify specific collateral or bind third parties**.

**After-acquired property:** an agreement **cannot automatically mortgage every future item simply by a broad phrase** unless the law and instrument support it; describe the **collateral class** and analyze **attachment, identification, replacement, and third-party effect**.
**Ownership of collateral:** a mortgagor generally must **own the property or be authorized to encumber it**.

The reviewer flags the **Revised Penal Code provision cited by the syllabus (Art. 319)** as the provision to check for **fraudulent or specific chattel-mortgage acts** in the fact pattern. The reviewer gives no elements or text for it — **verify the article itself** before applying it.

Foreclosure of a chattel mortgage follows **Act No. 1508**, including the statutory **notice and public sale procedures and application of proceeds**. The syllabus distinguishes **equity of redemption** under the law from **“no right of redemption” after a completed sale**, subject to any special rule.

blocks.markdown: **Exam trap:** in **installment sales governed by the Recto Law**, Art. 1484's **bar on deficiency recovery after the seller elects foreclosure** is critical — but it does **not automatically apply to every ordinary chattel mortgage securing a loan**. For installment sales, **test Recto Law coverage before deciding whether a deficiency is barred**.
